نِصَاحَاتٌ Skins. (S, K.) As cites as an ex this verse of El-Aasha, “فَتَرَى القَوْمَ نَشَاوَى كُلَّهُمْ
مِثْلَمَا مُدَّتْ نِصَاحَاتُ الرُّبَحْ
” (S, &c.) ربح here signifies, accord. to some, a young camel such as is called رُبَعٌ: (Az;) or a lamb, or kid: (ISd:) or the bird called in Persian زاغ. (TA.) [But see what follows.] ―
-b2- Also, (accord. to El-Muärrij, TA.) Snares, (as in some copies of the K, and in the TA) or cords, (as in other copies of the K) having loops (حَلَق) made to them, which are set, and with which apes (قُروُد) are caught; (K;) one of these animals being attached to one of the cords to attract others. (TA.) Agreeably with this signification some explain the verse of El-Aasha cited above; رُبَحٌ, originally رُبَاحٌ, signifying apes. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
